title.narrative: Mine Clearance and Organic Rice Development in Preah Vihear Cambodia

description.narrative:
Cambodia is one of the most mine-affected countries in the world, with an estimated 800km² of its land still contaminated. This situation presents a significant humanitarian challenge, as mine-related accidents compromises the safety of Cambodians. High levels of land contamination also raise a socio-economic challenge by preventing land use for agriculture and other economic activities.
The proposed Development Impact Bond (DIB) seeks to address the challenges through a holistic approach that integrates mine action with agricultural development. As the first-ever impact bond in the mine action sector, the DIB will foster a synergy between mine clearance and agricultural development through outcomes incentives. It will also serve as a proof of concept for future scalability and replicability in Cambodia and other-mine affected countries.

Communities are safer and are able to thrive Farming households obtain an increase in their net income from producing and selling organic rice Communities see an improvement in livelihoods and a reduction in poverty

The DIB’s target population consists of small-holder rice farmers from the three target villages (Pnov, Kdak, and Kantout) in Preah Vihear who cannot optimize their rice farming activities, because their rice farms are in mine affected areas, and because they have no access to good quality inputs and support services. These lead to yields and farm income that are currently below the average.
